diagnostics.message: The Lambda function is created before its Terraform-managed CloudWatch log group. On first invocation Lambda can auto-create `/aws/lambda/<function-name>`, racing the later `aws_cloudwatch_log_group.pool` creation and causing an already-exists conflict. The log group must exist first; because its current name references the Lambda resource, the name should also be decoupled from that reference to avoid a dependency cycle.

The pool Lambda can be invoked by the schedule before its execution role has the core `aws_iam_role_policy.pool` inline policy attached. The function should be ordered after this role policy so its runtime permissions are present before invocation.

The Lambda's execution role can lack the CloudWatch Logs inline policy when the function is created/invoked. `aws_iam_role_policy.pool_logging` should be established before the function is usable; note that the existing log-group name reference currently makes the overall ordering cyclic, so that reference also needs to be refactored.

When tracing is enabled, the Lambda can be invoked before `aws_iam_role_policy.pool_xray` has granted the execution role its X-Ray permissions. The function should be ordered after the conditional X-Ray role policy.

For a VPC-attached Lambda, the execution role needs `AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole` before the function creates/manages its ENIs. When `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role` is created, the Lambda function must depend on that attachment.

When the AMI ID SSM parameter is configured, the Lambda needs the SSM read policy at runtime. The function should be ordered after `aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read` so the attachment exists before any scheduled invocation.

The schedule can start invoking the pool Lambda as soon as it is created, but the scheduler execution role's invoke permission is in `aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler`, which Terraform may still be attaching. The schedule should depend on that role policy before becoming active.
